related_resources.reason: Dedekind cuts, publication in 1872, Cantor alternative.
Cauchy, Weierstrass and Dedekind, nineteenth-century analytical rigor.
Real number construction, completeness and sequences.
MIT 18.100B, lectures 1–7: completeness and convergence of real sequences.

historical_claims.anchor: Richard Dedekind developed a systematic way

prerequisites.reason: The rational-gap example and completeness discussion distinguish convergence to a point from internal Cauchy agreement; monotone and subsequence arguments use limits of real sequences.

recommended.reason: The irrationality argument uses a reduced-fraction assumption, parity, and contradiction; familiarity with those proof patterns helps separate an exact impossibility from numerical evidence.

background: Rational arithmetic, squares, parity, reduced fractions, and order inequalities. Cauchy sequences, suprema, and real completeness are introduced here; the bisection illustration previews continuity rather than assuming a completed continuity course.
readiness_checks: Can you state what it means for a real sequence to converge, including the order of the epsilon and N choices?
Can you explain why the bounded sequence alternating between 1 and minus 1 need not converge?
Can you explain why a fraction can be put in lowest terms and why the square of an odd integer is odd?

description: Builds real-number completeness from the missing rational square root of two, Cauchy sequences and least upper bounds, then uses it to justify monotone convergence, nested intervals and certified bisection.
